functional.root_cause: both stem from zeroconf setsockopt(IPV6_MULTICAST_IF) returning ENOPROTOOPT under qemu user-mode emulation; rest_command then fails to build a session and HA enters recovery mode. Native x86_64 on the same deb passes 30/30.

qemu_syscall_limitation.aarch64:
has_ipv6: True
idx=1 lo       IPV6_MULTICAST_IF FAILED errno=92 Protocol not available
idx=2 eth0     IPV6_MULTICAST_IF FAILED errno=92 Protocol not available
qemu_syscall_limitation.x86_64:
has_ipv6: True
idx=1 lo       IPV6_MULTICAST_IF ok
idx=2 eth0     IPV6_MULTICAST_IF ok
qemu_syscall_limitation.explanation: IPV6_MULTICAST_IF returns ENOPROTOOPT under qemu user-mode emulation but works natively. zeroconf sets it unconditionally, so the aiohttp resolver fails, which breaks rest_command and trips HA recovery mode. Not a property of the trimmed tree and not expected on real ARM64.

boundary: aarch64 is qemu-user emulation on an x86 host, not the target board. The 2 failing checks are traced to an emulation syscall limitation; the same deb passes 30/30 on native x86_64.
frontend_http_note: Observed HTTP 200 shortly after startup; the later probe in this same run hit connection-refused because HA logged "Pending HTTP config was not confirmed within 0:05:00; reverting to the stable config and restarting" and restarted itself, and the restarted process did not come back under qemu emulation. Not a packaging defect.
